purpose: HOST01 for puae6.wbx: what the objects of the engine, the portable host port, the bridge and the guest adapter import from libc and from the C++ runtime. The deterministic profile has no clock, file, process, thread, network or dynamic loading, so none of those may appear; tools/build_waterbox.py audit_imports fails the build on any name outside this list. Measured with llvm-nm on the objects of the link: 37 libc and C++ runtime names plus the emulibc heap service.

notes.exceptions: Only build/upstream/newcpu.cpp throws and catches (the 68000 core models its exceptions with C++ exceptions). Unwinding inside Waterbox is shown by p6w_probe_exception (T19b, tests/waterbox-smoke/test_puae6.py): an exception thrown 40 frames down is caught and every destructor on the way runs. The A500 profile never reaches the core's own throw (hardware_exception2 sets hardware_bus_error for a compatible 68000), so the probe is the evidence, not a run of the machine.
notes.math: sinf, cosf and powf are Paula's filter math (audio_math.cpp). Their results come from the musl and compiler-rt of the pinned sysroot, not from the host libm; T19c compares the PCM with headless.
notes.emulibc: alloc_sealed is the Waterbox runtime's own service (references/machawk/waterbox/emulibc): the firmware and the media are copied into the sealed heap during p6w_init. alloc_plain and alloc_invisible are not used: everything else is malloc, which Waterbox captures. __wbxsysinfo is the layout the runtime writes into the guest (the ranges of its heaps); p6w_memory_info hands it to the host.
